description: A General-purpose Task-parallel Programming System in C++

summary.one_liner: Taskflow is a header-only C++20 library for writing task-parallel programs, where you describe work as a graph of tasks with dependencies and an executor runs it across CPU threads (and GPUs via CUDA).
summary.what_it_does: Taskflow lets you create tasks and declare dependencies between them, such as running task A before B and C in parallel and D after both. You submit the graph to a tf::Executor, which runs it once, several times, or until a condition is met, and can return futures to query or wait on execution status. Asynchronous tasks can also be submitted directly to the executor. The graph can be dumped in DOT format for visualization with GraphViz. The README states it supports CUDA (nvcc) and Intel oneAPI DPC++ compilers and works on Linux, Windows, and macOS. The README includes only a short snippet of the API and points to external documentation and a cookbook for details.
use_cases: parallelize a C++ program across multicore CPUs
run tasks on GPUs with CUDA
schedule heterogeneous CPU and GPU workloads
visualize parallel task graphs as DOT diagrams
how_to_run: Include the Taskflow header in a C++20 program (header-only, no build of the library itself is described)
Create a tf::Executor and a tf::Taskflow
Add tasks with taskflow.emplace and define dependencies with precede/succeed
Run with executor.run(taskflow), run_n, or run_until, then call get() or wait_for_all()
Compile with a C++20 compiler, e.g. g++ -std=c++20
notable: Header-only library; include and use without linking a separate library
Describes work as a task dependency graph run by an executor
Supports one-shot, repeated, and conditional execution of a graph
Can dump task graphs to DOT format for visualization
Cites a 2022 IEEE TPDS paper for the underlying system
caveats: Requires a C++20-capable compiler with minimum versions listed (e.g. GCC 11+, Clang 12+, MSVC 19.29+)
README does not detail platform-specific GPU setup beyond naming the CUDA toolkit requirement
